subject: Latency playbook: TTFT targets & streaming cadence options
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@finovate.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: TTFT & streaming questions

Karthik — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can size the pilot: 

Summary / targets
- TTFT target: ideally <= 250 ms for the first token from our web clients (US region). Absolute hard limit for production is 350 ms.
- Streaming: we need chunked responses for progressive render on web; mobile app team prefers WebSocket but web UX team likes SSE.
- Chunk cadence goal: UI team would like first chunk within 200 ms and subsequent chunks roughly every 150–300 ms for long responses.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency during peak is ~200 active users, but we can spike to 450.
- Throughput: average message length ~80 tokens, peak tokens/sec estimate ~45k.

Questions for Redwood
1) What setup (SSE vs WebSocket) gives the best TTFT in practice, and any trade-offs we should expect?
2) Do you recommend any per-route batching or must we disable batching for lowest TTFT?
3) Would a dedicated pilot pool be necessary to guarantee the TTFT targets during our load profile?
4) Any additional telemetry/SDK we should include to measure chunk cadence precisely?

Attached is a short CSV with our traffic profile (finovate_load_profile.csv). We'd like a short pilot: 48–72 hours of traffic to validate TTFT and chunk cadence.

Next steps: if you can reply with a proposed pilot plan and the minimal config needed (pool size, model variant, recommended streaming mode), we can loop in Legal/Procurement for DocuSign and SOC2 evidence.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Director, Product Engineering
Finovate


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@finovate.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: TTFT & streaming questions

Alicia — really helpful notes and thanks for the traffic CSV. High-level quick answers up front, then a proposed pilot plan below. CC'ing Laura (solutions) and Ben (SRE) to align on capacity and runbook.

Short answers / tradeoffs
- TTFT: WebSocket can shave a few ms on connection reuse for mobile (TLS handshake amortization), but for browser-based SSE we often see comparable TTFT once connection warm (SSE has slight edge for one-way server push simplicity). Both are viable.
- Batching: disable cross-request batching for routes where TTFT is critical. Internal per-request micro-batching (<=2 ms) is ok; larger batching increases TTFT variability.
- Dedicated pilot pool: recommended to isolate noise and guarantee SLOs for the run.
- Telemetry: we'll provide a small SDK snippet to report chunk timestamps and a tracing header so you can correlate UI render times with server chunks.

Proposed pilot (48 hours)
- Model: open-vicuna-like variant (redwood-7b-quant-v2) — low-latency, quantized path.
- Pool: 4x A100-equivalent accelerators reserved for Finovate pilot (configurable).
- Config: no request batching; KV prefix cache enabled; max concurrency per GPU set to 64; autoscale disabled for the run.
- Streaming: default to SSE for web (first-chunk warmup enabled) and a WebSocket route for mobile. We will provide both endpoints.
- Chunk cadence: we recommend server-side chunk flush target of first chunk <= 200 ms after request start, then subsequent chunk flushes at 150 ms cadence for sequences > 64 tokens.
- SLOs to validate: TTFT p95 <= 250 ms; tail p99 <= 350 ms; chunk cadence mean <= 220 ms.

Next steps (what we need from you)
1) Confirm pilot window (48 vs 72 hours) and the expected start date.
2) Confirm target max concurrency (you mentioned 450 spike — please confirm whether that's short burst vs sustained).
3) Provide the list of IP ranges we should whitelist for a dedicated pool and whether traffic will come from your EU region (we'll pin region to us-east).

Deliverables from Redwood
- Pilot runbook PDF and a short SDK snippet to measure chunk timestamps.
- A temporary dedicated pool endpoint + credentials.
- SOC2 summary and an audit contact (we'll include that in the packet for Procurement).

I'll have Ben draft the exact capacity sizing and Laura will put together the runbook. If that's all good, we'll get DocuSign for the short pilot agreement and schedule a kickoff.

-karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference


From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@finovate.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finovate.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: TTFT & streaming questions

Thanks Karthik — that plan looks good. A few clarifications from our infra and product teams: 

- Pilot window: go with 48 hours starting Dec 7, 08:00 PT.
- Concurrency: sustained peak expected 200, but we can see 450 bursts for ~90s during batch job completions. Treat 450 as a short burst.
- Region: all traffic will originate from us-east (no EU/Apac for this pilot).
- IPs: we'll provide a CIDR block and a small list of public egress IPs by Tuesday.

Procurement asks for: DocuSign link + SOC2 contact + a short list of permitted data retention during the pilot (we can accept ephemeral logs for 7 days).

I'll start the DocuSign process and route SOC2 questions to your security contact. Please add Diego from SRE if he should be on the runbook coordination.

Alicia


From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Pilot setup & runbook items

Karthik / Ben — looping Diego for SRE runbook items. I've attached the pilot_runbook_v1.pdf and security_questionnaire_finovate.xlsx to this thread for reference. 

Ben: can you draft the exact GPU allocation + per-GPU concurrency numbers? My initial thought: 4 A100 equiv, with max 64 concurrency/GPU, leaves room for your estimated spikes. If we see sustained > 200 active sessions we'll bump to 6 GPUs.

Diego: please add the checklist items below to the runbook:
- Whitelist CIDRs (from Finovate) on the pool firewall.
- Enable chunk timestamp tracing header (x-rd-chunk-ts).
- Retention policy: ephemeral request logs for 7 days, metrics retained for 90 days.
- Post-run: we will provide a CSV of chunk timestamps and aggregated TTFT metrics.

I'll draft the DocuSign agreement and attach the SOC2 summary.

-Laura
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference


From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@finovate.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: TTFT & streaming questions

All — good progress. Quick operational checklist before we kick off Dec 7: 
1) Finovate to share CIDRs and confirm the 48-hour start.
2) Procurement to review and sign the pilot DocuSign link (we'll email in the next 24h).
3) Ben/Diego to provision the 4x GPU pool and share endpoint + credentials with Alicia.
4) Laura to send pilot_runbook_v1.pdf and the SDK snippet to Alicia.

Ben / Diego: please prioritize the small telemetry hook (x-rd-chunk-ts) and the sample curl command for both SSE and WebSocket streaming so Alicia can smoke test client-side.

Alicia: once we have the CIDRs and you confirm the start time we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff to walk through the runbook and expectations.

Thanks — looking forward to validating the TTFT numbers.

-karthik
